newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam coffee trade slows to trickle, prices slip.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam coffee trade slows to trickle, prices slip.

text.p: Vietnam's robusta coffee prices have fallen this week in very quiet trade of just a few hundred tonnes, dealers said on Friday.
Some buyers were looking for prices as low as $1,160 per tonne FOB Saigon Port. Sellers were quoting prices of around $1,210.
A week ago the trading price was around around $1,260.
"People are looking at Indonesia. There's just not much interest in Vietnam right now," one dealer said.
Prices were expected to weaken further next month as supplies from the new crop in Dak Lak province began appearing.
Output from the new 1996/97 crop is expected to reach 270,000 tonnes, against an estimated total of between 200,000 and 230,000 from the 1995/96 crop.
